rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before real data; synthetic validation at real counts in five periods (two estimator flaws found and fixed as amendments); 34 replication periods; four natives (NE41, #12 judges, #51 roles, #44 leader); preprocessing and post-hoc variants; scorecard; frozen, guarded confirm script dry-run, not run. No holdout run, no conversation-state or message-position variant of the context term.
rationale.faithfulness: The decomposition holds in every period (F3 >= 0.57 in 34/34; agent constant largest in 34/34) and survives genre controls, raw features, dedupe variants and an agent-day ceiling. The context and register parts of the model are weak: the context term is small (0.011 in regime III), follows received chat more than own fill, gives no attribution gain, and does not predict the size of the erasure jump; one register (judging) is shared, #51 roles are not. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: Tells a monitor builder what to do: attribute on the agent's mean style over >= 5 messages (accuracy 0.63, chance 0.10), skip context-position corrections, expect single messages to be ~73% noise, and do not read a post-reset style change as a model swap. Bounds H46's style-as-state rival. Not validated on the holdout or as a swap detector (one 20-message leader).

one_line: Style is an agent constant (0.55 of non-day systematic variance; F3 0.72 in 34/34 periods); context fill adds 0.08 (0.01 in regime III) and removing it gains no attribution.

models.note: Agent field dominates; context and register terms small

raters.claim: Within a goal period, chat style is an agent constant plus noise: the agent constant is the largest unique share in 34/34 periods, context fill and assigned registers add small shares (u_C median 0.08, 0.011 in regime III), and context detrending gives no attribution gain (mean Delta_c -0.007 [-0.017, +0.003], excluding a gain >= +0.01). Excluded: #51 role-register test, G44 leader rank, post hoc PH1-PH3.
